title: Round 32 Georgia-Florida state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Georgia and Florida. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces (USGS GNIS Geocoder; staged-products DomesticNames text via tools/gnis_extract.py; cumulative candidate extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). Brasstown Bald and Britton Hill additionally carry Domestic Names per-ID identity checks. The shared Chattahoochee/Flint confluence point and the Hartwell/Lanier official-name-order decisions are recorded below.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature and the point lay inside the intended state. County/census divisions, consolidated-government records, historical places, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant. Screens use the official GNIS name ('Hartwell Lake', 'Lake Sidney Lanier', 'Saint Johns River').

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID and per-ID identity checks for Brasstown Bald (354839) and Britton Hill (1851954), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py. The current text layout carries no elevation columns, so the two summit elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values. The candidate extract file is cumulative across batches 7-15; this register is the frozen batch-15 evidence.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes and reservoirs (text class Reservoir for Hartwell/Lanier; Lake for Okeechobee and Lake George), Streams & Canals to Stream, and Summit to Summit.

A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline. Two distinct river records may share one GNIS primary point (the Chattahoochee/Flint confluence); both are stored at the returned point without adjustment.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

Georgia.title: Georgia statewide frame (Georgia-Florida batch)
Georgia.frameNote: Georgia-Florida batch: the Atlanta capital anchor (the existing atlanta city frame's city at statewide scale) is balanced with the per-ID Brasstown Bald high point (4,784 ft), the Hartwell and Lanier reservoirs seeded under their official GNIS name orders, and three river records: the Altamaha mouth plus the Chattahoochee and Flint, whose GNIS primary points coincide exactly at their Decatur County confluence. The Savannah River row lives in the South Carolina frame (batch 14, SC-associated mouth record) and is a corridor here.

florida.title: Florida statewide frame (Georgia-Florida batch)

Florida is the flattest frame in the atlas; its synthetic relief uses metre-scale amplitudes honestly at that scale.

identityDecisions.candidate: Chattahoochee River 354236 and Flint River 358207 — identical GNIS primary point
identityDecisions.decision: Both seeded. The two distinct Apalachicola former rivers' GNIS records share exactly one primary point (30.7088028, -84.8638097, Decatur County) — their confluence — on both USGS surfaces. Both rows store the returned point unadjusted; the gazetteer therefore shows two pins at one location, which is the faithful representation of the source rather than an error. The Apalachicola's own record is seeded at its Gulf mouth in Florida.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Neither point is a channel centerline; the coincidence is a source property, not a survey.

identityDecisions.candidate: 'Lake Hartwell' order under states=GA and states=SC; 'Lake Lanier' short form
identityDecisions.decision: Both seeded under the official GNIS name orders. 'Lake Hartwell' returned empty arrays in both states; 'Hartwell Lake' (356215, Stephens County GA) reproduces. 'Lake Lanier' returned only a subdivision; the reservoir is 'Lake Sidney Lanier' (322971, Forsyth). Continuing the Vermilion/Monroe/B-Everett-Jordan rule: seed the official order, never invent a short form.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The seeded points are not shorelines.

identityDecisions.decision: Recorded for provenance colour: Britton Hill (FL), Hawkeye Point (IA, batch 7), and Hoosier Hill (IN, batch 9) hold consecutive FEATURE_IDs in the same GNIS high-point record series. No identity weight is placed on the adjacency beyond identification.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Sequential IDs are not evidence of anything beyond a shared GNIS registration batch.

identityDecisions.decision: The Savannah's GNIS row was already seeded in South Carolina (batch 14) on its SC-associated mouth record; it remains a corridor in Georgia rather than being duplicated. Identity-safe candidates omitted under the starter-scope treatment.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Starter-scope omission is not a claim about feature importance or identity.

knownLimitations: Georgia and Florida are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by official name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so Brasstown Bald (4,784 feet) and Britton Hill (345 feet) elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values; GNIS identity rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction.

GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines; Florida's amplitudes are metres-scale because the state is genuinely flat.

State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include areas outside their state outlines (including Atlantic/Gulf waters and the Keys reach); no boundary geometry is claimed.
